clues.title: Plate: black with three white sections
text: Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters. The letters usually appear as **three white sections** through the blur.
Commercial vehicles use yellow licence plates.
Plates in newer coverage can be [white](https://maps.app.goo.gl/41BknjygGkkbi1CJ6) too.
NOTE: Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.

images.caption: Indonesian plates: new from 2022 (top) and old (bottom)

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Plates are black with white letters, which look like three white blocks through the blur. Commercial vehicles have yellow plates, and newer coverage can show white ones. Malaysia's black plates usually show two blocks.

differs.how: Black plates usually show two white sections

clues.title: Driving side: left
text: Indonesia drives on the **left**.
NOTE: Malaysia drives on the left, while the Philippines drives on the right.

images.caption: An Indonesian street with traffic driving on the left; the added sign shows two-way traffic

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Cars drive on the left. Malaysia also drives on the left, but the Philippines drives on the right.

clues.title: Road lines: white or yellow centre, white edges
text: Indonesia uses **white or yellow** centre lines. Outer lines will always be white. The centre lines will be solid or dashed.
In Generation 3 coverage, yellow centre lines are more rare, as Indonesia only recently started using this colour for its road lines.
NOTE: Malaysian road lines are always all white.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Centre lines can be white or yellow, solid or dashed, and edge lines are always white. Yellow is rarer in Gen 3 coverage. Malaysia's lines are always all white.

clues.title: Pole: round steel or concrete
text: Poles in Indonesia are typically round and made out of either [**steel**](https://goo.gl/maps/rnii3wodNEqzH2FDA)** **or **concrete**. Many of the steel poles are painted black, and also feature the **Indonesian flag colours on them**. The pole tops are usually either [even](https://goo.gl/maps/rnii3wodNEqzH2FDA) or [uneven](https://goo.gl/maps/jA77LfkLbiz5AbK37), depending on the region.
_You can learn more about regional poles in the region-guessing section._

images.caption: A red circle and arrow zoom in on a red-and-white painted pole base
A red circle and arrow zoom in on a red-and-white painted pole base

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles are round, steel or concrete. Many steel ones are painted black with the national flag colours. Pole tops are either even or uneven, depending on the region.

clues.title: Bollard: black-white blocks or yellow-black
text: Indonesia commonly uses these **black-and-white** square or circular bollards, as well as these **yellow-and-black** ones, which can also have a red reflector. Other designs can also be found.
NOTE: [UK-style bollards](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YP74qg3Qj8Ugogus9) are mostly found in Kalimantan.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Common bollards are black-and-white squares or circles, or yellow-and-black ones that may have a red reflector. UK-style bollards are mostly found on one big island.

clues.title: Waystone: yellow, angled, cutout at top
text: Usually yellow waystones that are angled towards the road, and have a cutout close to the top are unique to Indonesia. They include shorthand for three cities or towns, with the biggest one being on the top in the cutout section.
NOTE: Waystones in the Philippines are perpendicular to the road and have the text facing away from the road.

images.caption: Two yellow angled waystones with a cutout at the top, shown side by side

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow waystones angled toward the road with a cutout near the top, showing short names of three towns with the biggest on top. In the Philippines waystones stand square to the road, facing away.

differs.how: Waystones stand square to the road, text facing away

clues.title: Language: Dutch-style spelling like "televisi"
text: Indonesian can look very similar to Malaysian, however Indonesian has been influenced by **Dutch**, and Malaysian by English. These small changes in spelling may help differentiate the two.

An example is the word television in English, which translates to ‘televisi’ in Indonesian, similar to the Dutch word ‘televisie.’ In Malaysian, it translates to ‘televisyen’, more similar to English.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Indonesian looks like Malay, but is influenced by Dutch, not English. For example "televisi" (like Dutch "televisie") against Malay "televisyen".

clues.title: Banners: rows of red and white flags
text: You can find these rows of red and white **banners **all around Indonesia. Sometimes, [more colourful flags](https://goo.gl/maps/iFwjZBmEWCbEcbvU9) can be found.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Rows of red and white banners appear all over the country. More colourful flags sometimes appear too.

clues.title: Ads: cigarette ads in black or red
text: **Cigarette **ads can be found all over Indonesia, usually with a black or red colour scheme and around a price of 18,000 Rp. Keep an eye out for **illustrated graphic pictures**, and the word **‘PERINGATAN’**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Cigarette ads are everywhere, usually black or red with a price around 18,000 Rp. Look for the graphic warning pictures and the word PERINGATAN.

clues.title: Plate: motorcycles have front plates
text: Motorcycles in Indonesia have **front** licence plates, as opposed to other south-east Asian countries which do not.

images.caption: Motorcycle with a front plate, marked by the red arrow

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other South-East Asian countries.

clues.title: Currency: Rupiah (Rp)
text: The official Indonesian currency is the Rupiah **(Rp)**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Prices on signs use Rp, the Rupiah.

clues.title: Coverage: limited, none in the far east
text: Coverage in Indonesia is fairly limited. Notably, there is no coverage on Papua or adjacent islands, and coverage is sparse in areas such as Kalimantan, Aceh, Central Sulawesi and North Maluku.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Coverage is fairly limited. There is none in Papua or the nearby islands, and little in Kalimantan, Aceh, Central Sulawesi and North Maluku.

clues.title: Sign: kabupaten (regency) names
text: The names of 2nd level subdivisions, named **‘Kabupaten’ **or **‘Kab’ **for short, translating to regency, can be found all over Indonesia on various signs and billboards. Each province is split up into multiple Kabupatens, totalling to 417 which are covered by street view, and therefore applicable in Geoguessr. These are learnable with enough time and patience.
_See the resources section for more information._

images.caption: Red ovals circle the regency names (KAB, Kabupaten) on two signs

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Signs and billboards often show the second-level region, called Kabupaten or Kab (regency). 417 are covered, and with time they are learnable.

clues.title: Language: compass words in addresses
text: You can find the **cardinal directions** written on many addresses. They are as follows:
- North = Utara
- East = Timur
- South = Selatan
- West = Barat
- Central = Tengah
- Southeast = Tenggara

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Addresses often have compass words: Utara north, Timur east, Selatan south, Barat west, Tengah central and Tenggara southeast.

clues.title: Satellite dishes: tilt shows equator side
text: Satellite dishes can help you determine whether you are north or south of the **equator**. For example, if the satellite dish points north, you are most likely south of it, and vice versa. Additionally, they usually point towards the middle part of West Kalimantan. This lets you use the angle to determine which side of Indonesia you are in. Lastly the angle of the satellite dish can also tell you how far away from the equator you are.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A dish pointing north means you are probably south of the equator, and the other way round. Dishes aim near the middle of West Kalimantan, so the angle shows which side of the country you are on and how far from the equator.

clues.title: Sign: five-digit postal code
text: While kabupaten names appear significantly more often, a number of [signs](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UgV2DtQbn4qVDL9t5) also display the **postal code**. Postal codes are five digits long and grouped by their starting digit, ranging from 1xxxx in Jakarta to 9xxxx in Maluku and Papua.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Some signs show a five-digit postal code. The first digit grows from 1 in the capital to 9 in the far east.

clues.title: Pole: even or uneven top bar
text: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: [**even**](https://goo.gl/maps/DBHoERAvYjR6zQbk8)** and **[**uneven**](https://goo.gl/maps/i1CUqRxZzPzgqZ9p7). This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

images.caption: Green box: even top bar; red box: uneven top bar; blue Mixed box; the map shows where each type is more common

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles have either an even (symmetrical) or an uneven bar holding the insulators. Learning where each type is common helps with region guessing.

clues.title: Pole: extra long support on top
text: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an **extra long support** on the pole top. Sometimes, [two supports](https://goo.gl/maps/TqHWQVDtBYiexALq9) can be present.

images.caption: A red arrow points to the extra long support under the top bar
A big red arrow points to the extra long diagonal support under the top bar
A red arrow points to the extra long diagonal support under the top bar

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: On the islands east of Java, poles often have an extra long support on top, sometimes two.

clues.title: Pole: triangle under the horizontal bar
text: You can find these poles with a **triangle attachment** under the horizontal bar in the following regions.
NOTE: This does not apply to [stacked poles](https://goo.gl/maps/qmeRHfBzabUpZ8uu5).

images.caption: A red box marks the triangle support under the horizontal bar

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Some poles have a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in certain regions. This does not apply to stacked poles.

clues.title: Pole: indent on both sides
text: Poles with an **indent** on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the indent in the side of the pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, the capital area and Banten.

clues.title: Pole: trident-shaped top
text: **Trident** style pole tops are most commonly found in **Central Java** and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Trident-style pole tops are most common in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rare in southern and western Kalimantan, North Sumatra and Riau.

clues.title: Pole: extra attachment under the top bar
text: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an **extra attachment** right under the horizontal bar.

images.caption: A red arrow points to the extra attachment under the top bar
A red arrow points to the extra attachment under the top bar

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In North and Central Sulawesi and Gorontalo, pole tops often have an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

clues.title: Pole: even bar, uneven insulators
text: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is **even**, but features **uneven **insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: An even bar with one insulator on one side and two on the other is almost only found in North Sumatra.

clues.title: Pole: A-shaped support
text: Poles with a **support shaped like the letter A** are common in Kalimantan and the Nusa islands.
NOTE: A-frame poles can exist anywhere where the electrical wires are in a bend and need extra support. Use this tip with caution.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles with an A-shaped support are common in Kalimantan and the islands east of Java. A-frames can appear anywhere wires bend, so use with care.

clues.title: Pole: crossbar flat side facing away
text: Poles with the **flat part of the crossbar facing away** from the pole are common in Sulawesi.
NOTE: Usually, poles in Indonesia have the flat part of the crossbar [attached](https://maps.app.goo.gl/NRULcr17wky2Wskq9) to the pole.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Poles with the flat part of the crossbar facing away from the pole are common in Sulawesi. Elsewhere it is attached to the pole.

clues.title: Pole: thin black pole, blue-green tape
text: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually **light blue and green**. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

images.caption: A red circle zooms in on the blue-green tape on the thin black pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Thin black poles beside regular ones, with two pieces of tape near the top, usually light blue and green, in the east of Central Sulawesi. Rarely in northern South East Sulawesi.

clues.title: Pole: rectangle attachment on the top
text: You can find this **rectangle **attachment on the pole tops which is mostly unique to Bali. This appears with the Lesser Sunda Island [support beam](https://goo.gl/maps/2tNeMhvSXphqn48V7) as well.

images.caption: A small red circle marks the rectangle attachment on top of the pole

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A rectangular attachment on pole tops is mostly unique to Bali, often with the extra long support seen on the nearby islands.

clues.title: Pole: horizontal text painted on the pole
text: Pole paint with **horizontal text **on the pole is usually a good clue for Bali. It is usually **dark blue** on Bali but can be [light blue](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tfSezgbbQ1Q2yKsX8) or even [green](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DKjM3Q4WCXZhhD3y9).

images.caption: A blue sticker on a concrete pole, centre

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pole paint with horizontal text is a good clue for Bali. It is usually dark blue, but can be light blue or green.

clues.title: Pole: uneven top with two supports below
text: **Asymmetrical poles** with **2 supports** below the bar occur mainly on Sumatra and the southern part of Sulawesi. It is not commonly seen in Kalimantan or Java.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Uneven poles with two supports below the bar are mostly on Sumatra and southern Sulawesi, not Kalimantan or Java.

clues.title: Fences: painted white with blue or red
text: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Painted fences, mostly white with blue or red, are typical for Sulawesi.

clues.title: Bollard: black bottom, white middle, yellow top
text: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted **black **on the bottom, **white **in the middle, and **yellow **on the top.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Bollards painted black at the bottom, white in the middle and yellow at the top are unique to Central Sulawesi.

clues.title: Bridges: green paint on the sides
text: **Green** paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Green paint is often on the sides of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

clues.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
text: Within Indonesia, oil palm plantations are mostly concentrated in **Sumatra **and **Kalimantan**. Palm plantations can rarely be seen in Sulawesi.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Oil palm plantations are mostly in Sumatra and Kalimantan, and rarely in Sulawesi.

clues.title: Fields: rice mostly on the main island
text: The majority of rice production is concentrated in **Java**, but can sometimes be found in other provinces, namely South Sulawesi and South Sumatra. They can rarely be found in other provinces as well. For a full overview, see [this page](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data/production/id).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most rice is grown on Java, though some is in South Sulawesi and South Sumatra, and rarely elsewhere.

clues.title: Landscape: drier, low shrubby look
text: The Nusas are **drier **than other regions in Indonesia. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead lower and shrubbier.
NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The islands east of Java are drier, with lower, shrubbier, browner vegetation, getting drier towards the east. Sumba is driest. Java can look this dry too.

clues.title: Landscape: round green hills, palms or corn
text: **Very rounded green hills**, typically covered with clusters of palms, sugarcane or corn, are extremely common within the province of Gorontalo.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Very rounded green hills, covered in palms, sugarcane or corn, are extremely common in Gorontalo province.

clues.title: Landscape: savannah, white car in Gen 3
text: This **savannah** landscape is occasionally seen on north Sumba.
NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a [white car](https://goo.gl/maps/Dz8hDHNHviJTvKiCA).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A savannah landscape occasionally seen on north Sumba. In Gen 3 you always see a white car.

clues.title: Soil: white soil on top of red
text: Red soil with a layer of **white soil on top** of it is most commonly found in the Bangka Belitung islands. On these islands, the white soil can often be seen spilling onto the road.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Red soil with a layer of white on top is most common on the Bangka Belitung islands, where the white often spills onto the road.

clues.title: Roofs: tiled
text: Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of **Java**, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.
NOTE: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look [slightly different](https://goo.gl/maps/BpZ43LPt2nDBJrHD9). The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Tiled roofs are most common on Java, and sometimes in southern Sumatra, the islands east of Java and South Kalimantan. Tiles in South Kalimantan and Jambi look flatter and less rounded.

clues.title: Roofs: plain sheet metal in the north
text: Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are **not **found. They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Plain sheet metal roofs are more common towards the north, where tiled roofs are not found, mostly on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

clues.title: Roofs: symmetrical triangle with two slopes
text: **Sheet metal roofs** with this shape, a **symmetrical** triangular shape with **two levels of sloping**, can be found mainly in Sulawesi, but can be found elsewhere in Indonesia.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Sheet metal roofs with a symmetrical triangle shape and two levels of slope are mostly on Sulawesi, but appear elsewhere too.

clues.title: Roofs: horizontal slots in the triangles
text: These** horizontal slots** inside the **triangles **of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.
NOTE: They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Horizontal slots inside the triangles of roofs are almost unique to southern Sulawesi, rarely in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

clues.title: Roofs: very high-pitched peaks
text: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely **high-pitched peaks** on Sumba.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Distinct roofs with unusually high peaks are found on the island of Sumba.

clues.title: Houses: crown-like roof tips, carved stone
text: **Architecture in Bali** is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these [crown-like roof pinnacles](https://goo.gl/maps/9v5HBGbiGDczWKYn7), found everywhere in Bali. [Guardian statues](https://goo.gl/maps/CB1pcgrABdjsc3Y88) and [slit-drum towers](https://goo.gl/maps/xPNMsB3rqDjjWZi39) are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see [gates](https://goo.gl/maps/StCdo1UxpSMXfA388), [walls](https://goo.gl/maps/KF7GweCfsicZyQpN7), and other [intricately carved ornaments](https://goo.gl/maps/9DHCZvKStsqSXG8RA) built from this material.

images.caption: A thatched rice barn on posts, with a village welcome sign on the front

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Crown-like roof pinnacles, guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common on Bali, plus carved gates and walls of dark volcanic andesite stone.

clues.title: Roofs: boat-shaped with spires
text: West Sumatra features these distinct **boat-shaped** roofs.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Distinct boat-shaped roofs are found in West Sumatra.

clues.title: Roofs: boat-shaped, flatter, no spires
text: North Sumatra features similarly distinct **boat-shaped** roofs, however the roofs are **less angled** upward and they do not feature spires.
NOTE: These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: North Sumatra has boat-shaped roofs too, but less angled upward and without spires, mostly near Lake Toba.

clues.title: Roofs: made of wooden chips
text: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of **wooden **chips.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Unique roofs made of wooden chips are found on Kalimantan.

clues.title: Roofs: gable horns
text: Roofs with **gable horns** can be found most commonly in [South Sulawesi](https://maps.app.goo.gl/THNEUGSHTyvnPqjn8), [Riau](https://maps.app.goo.gl/5JbZ5ryhrAygBQDB9) and [Central and South](https://goo.gl/maps/6JtUHKh3dccA8cvw6) Kalimantan.
NOTE: Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Horns on the roof gables are most common in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan. They often go with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi.

clues.title: Houses: raised, saddle-shaped roofs
text: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called [Tongkonan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongkonan), that have **saddle-shaped roofs**. The houses themselves are also **elevated from the ground**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A small area of South Sulawesi around Rante Pao has Tongkonan houses with saddle-shaped roofs, lifted off the ground.

clues.title: Signs: churches and Christian signs
text: Indonesia is religiously a **Muslim **majority country, so seeing churches, and other Christian signs, is a good clue for these regions.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The country is mostly Muslim, so churches and other Christian signs point to the regions where Christians live.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 with antenna, main island
text: **Generation 3 antenna** coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 3 coverage with an antenna is most common on Java, especially East Java, and very rare near Denpasar on Bali. In the west it has been replaced by Gen 4.

clues.title: Google car: black Gen 3 car
text: Black Generation 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere in Indonesia, but is most common in **Sulawesi**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black Gen 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere, but is most common in Sulawesi.

clues.title: Camera: moiré-like glitch
text: This camera glitch, reminiscent of a **Moiré Pattern**, is found throughout Central Kalimantan.
_You can click on the image for a clearer view._

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A camera glitch that looks like a moiré pattern, seen throughout Central Kalimantan.

clues.title: Landscape: lake with island, mountains
text: The region around **Lake Toba**, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Mountains surround a lake with an island in the middle. Overcast coverage is common. This is the Lake Toba area.

clues.title: Landscape: karst formations
text: Eastern South Kalimantan features these **karst formations**, particularly along the highway into East Kalimantan.
NOTE: Similar karst formations can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi and West Sumatra.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Eastern South Kalimantan has karst rock formations, especially along the highway into East Kalimantan. Similar ones are in South Sulawesi and West Sumatra.

clues.title: Landscape: bay with mountains west, flat east
text: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the **west **of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the **east**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A bay facing slightly north-west with mountains to the west and a flat, built-up area to the east, just north of Palu.

clues.title: Roofs: steep palm-leaf roofs
text: **Steeply** **pitched** roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Steeply pitched roofs made of palm leaves are sometimes seen on Nias Island, southwest of North Sumatra.

clues.title: Google car: white SUV with black bars
text: A **white **SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof can rarely be seen in eastern Bali.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof is rarely seen in eastern Bali.

clues.title: Google car: black cab, men sitting in the bed
text: A **black cab** with men sitting in the truck bed can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

images.caption: Camera blur seen from the front (left) and back (bottom right), labelled in red

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A black cab with men sitting in the back of the truck can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

clues.title: Soil: red soil on small islands east of Sumatra
text: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Banga Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Red soil is often found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, east of mainland Sumatra.

clues.title: Palms: fan leaves, dense round crown, short
text: Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Palmyra palms have fan-shaped leaves in a dense round crown and are usually short. They grow in dry parts: the islands east of Java and South Sulawesi.

clues.title: Palms: fan leaves, open crown, taller
text: Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Footstool palm has fan leaves like Palmyra, but the crown is more open, the leaves thinner and the palm taller. Mostly Sulawesi, rarely elsewhere.

clues.title: Palms: very large stiff upright fan leaves
text: Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Gebang palms have larger, stiffer, more upright leaves than the other fan palms. They flower once at the end of their life. Mainly Sulawesi and the islands east of Java.

clues.title: Plants: cassava with hand-shaped leaves

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Cassava has small hand-shaped leaves, grown in plantations or half-wild near houses. Most common in Lampung and Java, with Lampung the hotspot.

clues.summary: A small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers, found in dry regions: the islands east of Java and parts of Java and Sulawesi.

clues.summary: White leadtree has delicate feathery leaves and often visible bean pods. It grows mainly on the dry islands east of Java and a few other dry areas.
